items.a: ICHI Rating is a hero evaluation index that measures how frequently each hero was played by the players who ranked on the Overwatch 2 competitive Top 500 leaderboard. Each region kept its own Top 500 leaderboard, so the index reflects the most-played heroes at the top of the ladder in Asia, Europe, and the Americas.

The system crawled the Top 500 leaderboard once a day and checked each player's three most-played heroes. The 1st most-played hero received 3 points, the 2nd received 2 points, and the 3rd received 1 point. These scores were summed across all Top 500 players in each region to produce that day's ICHI Rating.

ICHI Rating has not been updated since Overwatch 2 Season 20 (December 2025). Before that it was collected and refreshed once a day from January 2024 onward, so the chart below is a daily record of Season 19 and earlier, kept as an archive. Nothing new is added to it, and the values already in it do not change.

items.q: Why is ICHI Rating no longer collected?
items.a: Overwatch 2 Season 20 (December 2025) changed what the leaderboard ranks players by. Through Season 19 the competitive Top 500 leaderboard ranked the best players by competitive rank; from Season 20 the ranking is by Challenger score, which the Challenger system tallies for players at Diamond and above and which builds up as they keep winning. That is a different basis from the one ICHI Rating was built on, so the two cannot be continued as one index, and collection ended with the last snapshot taken before Season 20. The archive that remains covers January 2024 through December 2025, describing Overwatch through Season 19 rather than the current meta.

items.q: How should I interpret the chart?
items.a: A higher ICHI Rating means the hero collected more points from that region's Top 500 players that day, where each player gave 3 points to their most-played hero, 2 points to their second and 1 point to their third. A hero therefore rises both when more players keep it among their three most-played heroes and when it sits higher within them. Sudden spikes often correspond to balance patches or meta shifts. Comparing heroes across regions reveals how the meta differed between Asia, Europe, and the Americas.
